profile.reading:
This facility is attributed to the Virginia Information Technologies Agency, known as VITA, the executive-branch agency that provides centralized information technology services to Virginia state government, and is located at 11751 Meadowville Lane in Chesterfield County, in the Richmond metropolitan area. VITA was established in 2003 to consolidate and manage IT infrastructure and services across Virginia's executive branch agencies, along with, in varying capacities, local governments and higher education institutions. In 2010, legislation signed by Governor Bob McDonnell restructured the agency, placing it under the Secretary of Administration and replacing its former independent oversight board with an Information Technology Advisory Council, while its billing rates continue to be reviewed by the state's Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission.

For roughly a decade and a half after its founding, VITA's infrastructure, including data center operations, was managed under a large outsourced contract with Northrop Grumman. That single-vendor arrangement ended around 2018, when the Commonwealth settled with Northrop Grumman for 35.8 million dollars and, following a September 2018 executive order from Governor Ralph Northam directing agencies toward cloud-based platforms, moved to a multi-supplier IT services model. VITA has continued to modernize since: it deployed Virginia's first end-to-end robotic process automation service in July 2021 and rolled out a multiplatform secure messaging option the same year, and by 2020 it had drawn national recognition from NASCIO, the National Association of State Chief Information Officers, for its enterprise IT management program.

This Chesterfield County site appears in Virginia Department of Environmental Quality air permit records as a listed data center location, which is consistent with an active, operating facility with on-site backup generation, since standby generators are what typically trigger air-permit requirements for a building of this kind, rather than with an office or administrative address. No published square footage, IT capacity in megawatts, or construction date specific to this Meadowville Lane building was found in the sources reviewed. VITA's main administrative address is 7325 Beaufont Springs Drive in Richmond, a separate location from this data center site, underscoring that this Chesterfield County facility functions as operational infrastructure rather than as the agency's public-facing headquarters.

reading.body:
This facility in Chesterfield County, Virginia is operated by the Virginia Information Technologies Agency, a state government IT department established in 2003. It sits in a state where 326 mapped data centers have been identified, but only 23 publish their capacity figures. No megawatt capacity is published for this campus.

Because this facility publishes no power specification, its scale cannot be assessed against Virginia's 1,375 MW of published capacity across the state. The operator is a public agency serving Virginia's state and local government entities and higher education institutions rather than a commercial cloud or AI infrastructure provider. Without a published figure, this facility cannot be ranked among Virginia's disclosed capacity.

For a reader evaluating whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the published record contains no evidence of AI-relevant infrastructure. The operator's mandate and historical focus on government IT services, cloud consolidation, and robotic process automation do not indicate current involvement in large-scale compute for AI training or inference. Any capacity this facility holds is not documented in sources this site has reviewed.
